featured_reviews.review_text:
it is a refreshing green oasis in the midst of Mumbai’s bustling urban landscape. For nature lovers and those looking to escape the city’s hectic pace, this reserved forest offers a peaceful retreat where you can reconnect with nature.

Natural Beauty:
The forest is lush and full of greenery, with a variety of trees and plants that create a tranquil atmosphere. It’s an ideal spot for morning walks, jogging, or simply enjoying a quiet moment surrounded by nature. The air is noticeably fresher here, providing a welcome break from the city’s pollution and noise.

Wildlife and Flora:
While the forest is relatively small, it is home to a diverse range of flora and fauna. Birdwatchers, in particular, will enjoy spotting various species of birds that frequent the area. The forest’s rich biodiversity adds to its charm, making it a great spot for anyone interested in nature and wildlife.

Accessibility:
it is conveniently located in Chembur, making it easily accessible for residents of the area. The pathways are well-maintained, making it a pleasant place to explore on foot. However, the signage within the forest could be improved to help visitors navigate the trails more easily.

Maintenance:
The forest is generally well-kept, but there are areas where maintenance could be enhanced. Some parts of the forest could benefit from more regular cleaning, as litter can occasionally be found along the trails. Additionally, more seating areas or benches would be a nice addition for visitors who want to rest and take in the scenery.

Conclusion:
it is a delightful green space in Chembur that offers a much-needed escape into nature.

featured_reviews.name: Derishta Pillay
featured_reviews.review_text:
At the outset I must say that neither myself nor my husband are huge fans of the usual guided walking tours mainly because we hate being taken to cliched and crowded tourist hotspots, listening to facts straight from the Wikipedia page and jostling for space with other tourists just to return sunburned and underwhelmed. In addition we'd already spent a hectic 5 weeks in India - we were tired, grumpy, waiting to fly back home and not at all looking forward to our last 4 days in Mumbai at all. So basically when our travel companions insisted we book a tour - the scene was set for disaster...
'Bombay Walks' single handedly turned this around and Mumbai actually turned out to be the highlight of our trip! (Nope this is not a sponsored review 😂)

The tour: Arpan's tour extends to the days before and after the actual tour as he offers valuable advice about where to stay/eat/party/shop etc. He speaks perfect English, is pleasant and very easy to communicate with. His passion and love for the city is infectious and you will end his tour enthralled, overwhelmed and completely charmed by Mumbai and it's people - vowing to come back and dig deeper, spend longer and see more. The city tour covers many facets of the city - traveling to hidden gems and local landmarks across the length and breadth of Mumbai. You get to see and experience aspects of Mumbai that you'd never be able to do alone with a guide book or google maps - like traveling on local trains and walking through Worli fishing village and stopping by at small off-the-beaten path temples and churches.

The guide: Arpan is reliable, trustworthy and comes well prepared for the type of group. His talking style is light-hearted and easy going but still knowledgeable and always engaging. He's the type of guide that can tell you interesting facts about the history, architecture and politics of a place but also where to get the best coconut water along the way and which public toilets are ok to use.
We only met Arpan in person on the day of the tour and although we were constantly bombarded with sights, sounds and smells (it is Mumbai after all) - it never once felt like we were just being dragged from point to point whilst he rattled off information but rather that we were spending the day walking around with an old friend.

Target travelers: We're fairly well travelled and yet this is the first time we've ever bothered to leave a tour review - on any platform - I think that in itself indicates how highly we recommend this tour.
This is really a 'must do' in Mumbai.
It's so good we would do this tour again even if it were to cover the exact route we already took. The walking wasn't particular strenuous so it's recommended for any age group it should also be noted that we found that     Arpan was discreetly always conscious of where the group members were and their safety and constantly aware of our surroundings and the locals around us - on that note I would recommend this tour even if you're a single female traveling alone.

When to do it: Try and do this tour on your first full day in Mumbai because it's also a great way to orientate yourself around the city and plan the rest of your time there.

That city that everyone talks about - that's all of India's many faces and layers in one, that accepts everyone, that's everyone's home - regardless of language, religion or creed - Mumbai is THAT city and you'd be crazy if you miss the opportunity to let a born-and-bred local guide you around...

Had an absolutely wonderful experience at Juhu Chowpatty! 🌊✨ The vibrant atmosphere, cool sea breeze, and stunning sunset views make it one of the best places in Mumbai to unwind. The beach is lively yet relaxing, perfect for evening walks with family and friends.

The street food is the real highlight – from delicious pav bhaji to mouth-watering pani puri and kulfi, every bite adds to the charm of the place. The energy, the sounds of the waves, and the buzzing food stalls create a truly iconic Mumbai experience.

A must-visit spot to feel the real spirit of the city! 🌅

featured_reviews.name: Dinesh Kumar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Juhu Chowpatty, popularly known as Juhu Beach, is one of the most famous tourist attractions in Mumbai. Located along the Arabian Sea, it is a lively and vibrant place that draws thousands of visitors every day. The beach is known for its golden sand, breathtaking sunsets, and refreshing sea breeze. People from all walks of life come here to relax, enjoy the waves, and spend quality time with family and friends.

One of the highlights of Juhu Chowpatty is its street food culture. The beachside stalls serve mouth-watering snacks such as bhel puri, pani puri, pav bhaji, and sev puri, making it a paradise for food lovers. The aroma of freshly prepared food adds to the charm of the place. During evenings, the beach becomes even more colorful with lights, laughter, and cheerful crowds.

Juhu Chowpatty also holds cultural and social importance. It is a venue for festivals like Ganesh Visarjan, where thousands gather to immerse idols with great devotion. The area around the beach is home to several celebrities, adding to its popularity.

featured_reviews.name: Arjun Pitroda
featured_reviews.review_text:
​Juhu Chowpatty is a landmark for Mumbaikars, but for cyclists taking the coastal route, it serves as a crucial pitstop, especially the stretch near the Santacruz side where the beach meets the main road.

​I often pull over here on my morning rides for a quick break and a necessary blast of fresh sea air. The convenience of stopping right by the road is unbeatable, and even when the city is bustling, you can usually find a spot to lean your bike and just breathe for a few minutes.

​The experience is definitely hit or miss, and I recommend managing expectations regarding cleanliness. Sometimes the sand is reasonably clean and perfect for a morning walk, but other times, especially after heavy tides or busy days, it can be quite messy. The breeze, however, is consistently refreshing.

​If you’re looking for a quick activity, you’ll find plenty of folks offering short boat rides along the water's edge. It adds a lively, commercial buzz to the area.

​Overall, it's a reliable, easily accessible coastal stop. Not always pristine, but always offering that essential Mumbai sea vibe and a decent spot for a cycling break.

​Pro Tip for Cyclists: Time your visits for early mornings before the crowds arrive to enjoy the best air quality and quietest atmosphere.

featured_reviews.name: Chirag
featured_reviews.review_text: Juhu Beach offers a beautiful and scenic coastline, especially during sunset, making it a great place to relax and enjoy the sea breeze. However, the main Juhu Chowpatty area is usually very crowded and not very clean, which can take away from the overall experience. If you walk further away from the Chowpatty zone, you’ll find relatively cleaner and less crowded stretches where you can enjoy the beach more peacefully. Motor boat rides are also available, typically quoted at ₹300 per person, but if you’re in a group, you can negotiate the price down to around ₹100 per person or even less. Despite the crowd and cleanliness issues, it’s still worth visiting for its lively atmosphere and scenic views.

The food lane near the beach is packed with stalls selling gola, pav bhaji, falooda, chaat, and juices, all glowing under bright lights.
Crowds keep the place buzzing, and the atmosphere feels like a mini food festival every evening.
The ice-gola shops with their rows of colorful syrup bottles look amazing and instantly pull you in.
Service is quick even when it’s crowded, and the staff handle customers with calm and speed.
The variety of food is huge, and everything smells tempting the moment you step in.
The beach itself is lively, full of families, kids, and tourists enjoying the sea breeze.
It can get crowded, but that crowdedness feels like Mumbai’s signature heartbeat.
Great place for street food lovers and for capturing fun, vibrant photos.
If you want to feel the true Mumbai spirit, Juhu Chowpatty in the evening is the perfect spot.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Dhobi Ghat for a college street photography project, and honestly, it turned out to be one of the most visually fascinating places I’ve explored in Mumbai. The scale of it all instantly catches your attention — endless rows of clothes, synchronized movement, narrow lanes, textures, colours, and stories unfolding in every corner.

For photography, the place is a goldmine. Every frame feels layered with life, hard work, and rhythm. There’s chaos, but there’s also incredible structure hidden within it. “Beauty lies in the ordinary,” and Dhobi Ghat reflects exactly that through its everyday reality.

What I appreciated most was how authentic and unfiltered the entire place felt. Raw Mumbai in its truest form.

featured_reviews.name: Donggeon Kang
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dhobighat has been operating since 1890 during British colonial rule. From early dawn well past sunset the Dhobi Wallahs work tirelessly washing laundry collected from all across Mumbai. Learning that these workers are considered untouchables  people who fall outside even the caste system. left me standing on that bridge in silence feeling a weight I couldn’t quite shake.

Thousands of years of caste hierarchy pressed into every concrete washing pen. That image stayed with me long after I left.

What struck me most was the view from above. Gleaming luxury high rises tower directly behind this open air laundry where people labor by hand all day for almost nothing. That contrast is not just striking, It is Mumbai in one frame. It is India in one frame.

Come here not just to see it but to feel what it means.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

featured_reviews.review_text: Mahalaxmi Dhobi Ghat is a famous open-air laundry in Mumbai, India, established in 1890. featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Udyan and Zoo (Rani Chi Baug) recently. The zoo is a good place for a family outing and children can enjoy seeing various animals and birds. The garden area is green and peaceful, making it suitable for a short walk.

However, some sections could be better maintained, and a few animal enclosures appeared smaller than expected. Due to crowds, especially on weekends, the overall experience can feel a bit rushed. Facilities and signboards could also be improved for visitors.

Overall, it’s a decent place to spend a few hours in Mumbai, particularly for families with kids, but there is room for improvement.

featured_reviews.name: ameya mahadik
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a fantastic visit to Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Botanical Udyan and Zoo. The place offers a perfect blend of nature, history, and wildlife. The botanical garden is lush, well-maintained, and home to a wide variety of trees and plants, making it a refreshing escape in the heart of Mumbai.

The zoo is equally impressive, with a good collection of animals including tigers, hippopotamuses, crocodiles, deer, and many other species. The biggest attraction for me was the penguin enclosure. Seeing penguins up close was a unique experience and one of the major highlights of the visit.

The premises are clean, the animal enclosures are well organized, and there is plenty of information available for visitors. It's a great destination for families, children, wildlife enthusiasts, and anyone looking to spend a day surrounded by nature.

Overall, it was an enjoyable and memorable experience, and I would highly recommend visiting if you're in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Rohit Parui
featured_reviews.review_text: I absolutely love Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Botanical Udyan and Zoo. I highly recommend everyone to go and spend some quality time here with friends, family, and kids. It is a wonderful place where you can see a rich variety of different birds, animals, and beautiful trees. Beyond just being a fun day out, it is incredibly educational for kids as they can easily gain a lot of knowledge about nature and wildlife while exploring the beautiful grounds..

featured_reviews.name: Abir Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
The place is well-maintained, but it feels more like a garden than a proper zoo due to the limited number of animals. There is only one tiger and one leopard, and several key animals are missing—there are no elephants, lions, or giraffes. The bird section also has very few species, although penguins are available, which is a plus.

The area is clean and spacious, and the food options inside are good. However, basic facilities like access to cold drinking water should be improved. Considering the large number of visitors and the strong revenue potential, the management should focus on adding more animals and enhancing overall maintenance to make the experience more worthwhile.

featured_reviews.name: Uday Pasupuleti
featured_reviews.review_text: Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Botanical Garden and Zoo is a wonderful attraction in Mumbai, combining beautiful greenery with an exciting wildlife experience. The garden is well maintained with lush landscapes, rare plants, and majestic old trees that make every walk refreshing. The zoo's major attractions include the penguins, Bengal tiger, leopard,Hippo,Bear, crocodiles, monkeys, deer, and a variety of colorful birds. Watching the penguins is especially a delight for both children and adults. The entire facility is clean, organized, and educational, making it an ideal destination for families, nature lovers, and photographers. A must-visit place to enjoy nature and wildlife in the heart of Mumbai

Good to see water fountains all around and decently maintained animal shelters... the children park is a good size albeit with quite a few swings broken and not well maintained... look into that please so kids can have thier share if fun

featured_reviews.name: Aditee Kale
featured_reviews.review_text:
VeerMata Jijabai Bhosale Udyan is a perfect place to visit for an enjoyable zoo experience in Mumbai. The zoo is well-maintained and offers a chance to see a wide variety of animals in a pleasant and engaging environment.

It houses animals such as tigers, leopards, sambar deer, barking deer, turtles, tortoises, and many more providing a great learning and viewing experience for visitors of all ages. There is also a dedicated bird park with multiple species of birds, including parrots and other colorful varieties, which is especially delightful. Everywhere there are information boards talking about that specific animal or bird, which becomes helpful for people to know what they are and what are the special / interesting facts about them.

One of the major attractions is the separate, temperature-controlled enclosure for penguins, which is very well designed and adds to the uniqueness of the zoo.

Additionally, the zoo has an in-house canteen that serves good food with a variety of options, including Indian and Chinese cuisine, juices, and chaat, making it convenient for visitors to relax and refuel during their visit.

Overall, it is a great place to spend quality time with family, kids and enjoy a refreshing day close to nature.

customer_updates.text:
Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Museum is the oldest museum in Mumbai. Situated in the vicinity of Byculla Zoo, Byculla East, it was originally established in 1855 as a treasure house of the decorative and industrial arts.

The museum was opened on 2 May 1872 as The Victoria and Albert Museum, Bombay. A little more than a hundred years later, on 1 November 1975, the museum was renamed the Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Museum in honour of the man whose vision and dedication enabled its establishment. Bhau Daji Lad was the first Indian Sheriff of Mumbai, a philanthropist, historian, physician, surgeon and secretary of the Museum Committee when it was first instituted

There were also many artifacts from ancient India on display, including plates, soap stands, utensils, and several other historical items. The collection is vast and well maintained, making it a fascinating place to explore for anyone interested in history and culture.

featured_reviews.name: Anagh Pathak
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Museum, located within the verdant enclave of the Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Udyan (Byculla Zoo), is Mumbai’s oldest museum and a masterpiece of Victorian design. Opened to the public in 1872 as the Victoria and Albert Museum, it was originally conceived to showcase the industrial arts and the rich cultural heritage of the Bombay Presidency. The building itself is an architectural treasure, featuring a stunning Palladian exterior and an opulent interior characterized by intricate Minton tile floors, gilded pillars, and an ornate ceiling. Following an extensive restoration in the early 2000s, it became a cultural beacon, winning the prestigious UNESCO Award of Excellence for heritage conservation.

The museum’s collection offers a meticulous historical narrative of Mumbai’s evolution from a cluster of seven islands into a bustling colonial metropolis. The galleries house an extraordinary array of clay models, dioramas, and maps that illustrate the city’s early social life, traditional costumes, and diverse communities. One of the most famous exhibits is the massive basalt elephant sculpture, dating back to the 6th century, which was originally found on Elephanta Island and moved to the museum grounds in the 1860s. These artifacts provide a rare, tangible link to the craftsmanship and daily rhythms of a bygone era, making it an essential destination for history enthusiasts.

Situated amidst the lush botanical gardens of the zoo, the museum serves as a serene cultural sanctuary away from the city's modern chaos. It frequently hosts contemporary art exhibitions, educational workshops, and film screenings, bridging the gap between historical preservation and modern artistic expression. The surrounding plaza and the nearby David Sasoon Clock Tower add to the nineteenth-century charm of the precinct. By integrating the natural beauty of the Byculla Zoo with its high-Victorian grandeur, the Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Museum remains a vital institution that celebrates the artistic soul and the complex, multifaceted history of Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Liviu-Alexandru Buftea (Style)
featured_reviews.review_text:
An incredible testament to colonialism, resilience and ingenuity of the Indian people. It's hard to believe and explain all I learned. This museum is a must-see!

Come to see the rich extravagant beauty arose from a brutal exploitation of resources, for the sensitivities of some petty lords and governors.

An unprecedented exchange of ideas and culture, intertwined in ivory, wood, and sculpted on amphorae.

Discover a plethora of history, linking us to the beginning of civilization.

After visiting this museum I have a newfound love, understanding and respect of the Indian people, culture and history, and a newfound distaste from colonialism and exploitation, especially the British and Jewish kind.

I recommend to take a free tour, if one is formed. They have dedicated professionals, who put everything into context and give the visit a nice flow.
